Each of INV-1..INV-9 assessed APPLIES/NOT-APPLICABLE with reasoning

result.summary:
Scope test: APPLIES -- diff touches attachment byte-content access control (git diff main...HEAD: lib/letflow/repository/attachment_links.ex new, lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex +125, lib/letflow/api/{error,response,authorization}.ex changed) plus a new per-tenant secret (secrets table, namespace 'attachments'/name 'link_signing_key'). Continued to full invariant review, not an out-of-scope PASS.

INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES, SATISFIED. (a) Both new handlers (handle_issue_attachment_link/3, handle_get_attachment_link_content/3, instances.ex L1248-1349) source tenant_id exclusively from conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id and opts exclusively from conn.assigns.scoped_opts -- never from the token, query string, or request body; verify/3's tenant_id parameter is likewise always this same conn.assigns value, never a value decoded from the token (the token payload carries no tenant field at all -- confirmed by reading its JSON schema in attachment_links.ex L102-107/141-143). (b) Letflow.Secrets access goes through the module's own already-reviewed Secrets.resolve/2 and Secrets.put/2 -- no new Repo call, no bypass. (c) Secrets.resolve/2 (lib/letflow/secrets.ex L266-297) independently re-derives tenant match from the reference's own tenant_slug via Identity.get_tenant_by_slug/1 and compares it against opts[:tenant_id], returning {:error, :tenant_mismatch} on any mismatch or unknown tenant BEFORE the row query runs (L291-297) -- this is defense-in-depth beyond AttachmentLinks' own tenant_id sourcing, not a bypass. No caller-supplied tenant_id field exists anywhere in this diff (no migration; no new tenant_id column).

INV-2 (server-side field authorisation) -- treating as APPLIES (the security-invariants.md 'S4 not started' applicability note for INV-2/INV-5 is itself stale -- this codebase already has ~50 live API routes per lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex's own endpoint_policy_key/2 table, and Letflow.Api.Error's own moduledoc already cites REQ-072's INV-5 mechanism as shipped; flagging this staleness for DOC-UPDATER/ORCH the same way INV-1's 2026-08-17 correction was made, but not treating it as license to skip the check). SATISFIED: render_attachment_link/4 (instances.ex L1273-1281) hand-builds an explicit 5-key map (attachment_id, token, url, expires_at, expires_in_seconds) -- no raw struct/Jason.Encoder derivation, no secret-bearing field. The signing-key plaintext never reaches this function at all.

INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing) -- NOT APPLICABLE. No Lua/WASM/scripting surface touched.

INV-4 (secrets by reference only) -- APPLIES, SATISFIED. Traced every use of the signing-key plaintext variable in attachment_links.ex: bound as `plaintext` (create_signing_key/1 L192, get_or_create_signing_key/2 L180) or `signing_key` (resolve_signing_key/3 L215, sign/2 L232) and used ONLY as the second argument to :crypto.mac(:hmac, :sha256, signing_key, payload) (L232) or passed straight into Secrets.put/1's plaintext: field (L198, which is Letflow.Secrets' own already-reviewed encrypt-at-rest write path). Never logged (zero Logger/IO.inspect calls in the file), never returned from issue/3 (return value is %{token: token, expires_at: expires_at} at L115, token being base64(payload).base64(signature), not the key), never returned from verify/3 (returns {:ok, attachment_id} or {:error, :expired_or_invalid}), never placed in any response map (render_attachment_link/4's map above has no key-shaped field), never included in an error tuple ({:error, {:secret_write_failed, reason}} carries reason from Secrets.put/1's own return, which per Letflow.Secrets' own contract is a changeset/db-error term, not plaintext -- Secrets.put/1 is out of this diff's scope and was already security-reviewed). grep -rniE secret/token/key literal-hardcode heuristic against the new file: no hardcoded key material, only the namespace/name string constants "attachments"/"link_signing_key" (config-key names, not secret values).

INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability) / AC4 -- APPLIES, SATISFIED, independently re-derived from the shipped code (not from the design doc's or moduledoc's own claim):
  (a) verify/3's with/else structure (attachment_links.ex L138-155) has exactly one else-reachable failure path. Traced all six branches against actual Elixir semantics: (1) String.split(token, ".", parts: 2) returns a 1-element list on a token with no "." -- fails to match the 2-element [payload_b64, signature_b64] pattern, falls to else. (2)/(3) Base.url_decode64/2 returns the bare atom :error (not {:error, _}) on invalid base64 -- fails to match {:ok, payload/signature} <- ..., falls to else. (4) Jason.decode/1 (confirmed non-bang; verified this returns {:error, %Jason.DecodeError{}} rather than raising, per Jason's documented non-bang contract -- this file never calls Jason.decode!/1) -- a decode failure, or a decoded map missing any of the three required keys, or wrong value types, fails the guarded pattern `{:ok, %{...}} when is_binary(...) and is_integer(...) and is_integer(...)`, falls to else. (5) resolve_tenant_slug/1 returns {:error, :invalid_tenant} on an unknown tenant -- does not match {:ok, tenant_slug}, falls to else. (6) resolve_signing_key/3 itself already normalizes every Secrets.resolve/2 failure (:invalid_reference/:tenant_mismatch/:not_found/:purpose_not_allowed/:disabled/:deleted) to {:error, :expired_or_invalid} (L216) -- even though this already carries the right value, it still fails to match {:ok, signing_key} and falls to the same else clause, so there is no second distinct value in play. (7) :crypto.hash_equals/2 returning false -- fails `true <-`, falls to else. (8) expiry check returning false -- fails `true <-`, falls to else. All eight fall through to the single `else _ -> {:error, :expired_or_invalid}` (L150-151, one clause, one value) -- confirmed genuinely one return value reachable from every failure branch, not merely asserted.
  (b) Router ordering confirmed by reading handle_get_attachment_link_content/3 (instances.ex L1299-1327): the `with` chain calls verify_link_token/2 (which delegates to AttachmentLinks.verify/3) strictly before check_attachment_id_matches/2, which runs strictly before fetch_scoped_attachment_content/3 -- Elixir `with` clauses execute top-to-bottom and short-circuit on the first non-matching clause via `else`, so an earlier clause's failure genuinely never reaches a later clause. check_attachment_id_matches/2 (L1345-1348) also collapses its own single failure mode (decoded attachment_id != raw_attachment_id from the URL) to the identical {:error, :expired_or_invalid} value, not a distinct one -- confirmed by reading its two clauses (matching-pattern -> :ok; anything else -> {:error, :expired_or_invalid}). No intervening branch between verify_link_token/2 and fetch_scoped_attachment_content/3 varies behavior by which of the two prior failure causes fired -- both funnel through the same `else {:error, :expired_or_invalid} -> Response.attachment_link_expired(conn)` clause (L1315-1316).
  (c) Checked actual arity/signature, not the moduledoc's description: Letflow.Api.Error.attachment_link_expired/0 (error.ex L221-229) takes zero arguments -- its detail string "This link has expired..." is a literal in the function body, no parameter. Letflow.Api.Response.attachment_link_expired/1 (response.ex L154-155) takes only `conn`; its body is `send_problem(conn, Error.attachment_link_expired())` with no other argument threaded through. Confirmed: no caller-suppliable argument exists on either function -- structurally identical to not_found/0's INV-5 shape, which both docstrings correctly cite as the precedent.
  (d) Side-channel check, named explicitly as required:
    - Timing: verify/3's DB-round-trip count varies by failure class (0 round trips for a malformed/undecodable token; 1 for resolve_tenant_slug alone if that somehow failed; 2 -- resolve_tenant_slug + resolve_signing_key -- for a syntactically well-formed token that fails signature or expiry). This IS a real timing differential, but it is NOT an INV-5-relevant signal: tenant_id is sourced from the requester's own already-authenticated auth_context, never from the token or from anything attacker-influenced, so this round-trip count is a function of 'is my own request well-formed', constant for a given authenticated caller regardless of which attachment_id, which tenant's token, or a wholly fabricated attachment_id is embedded in the payload. A cross-tenant-presented (real) token and a token naming a never-issued attachment_id both take the identical path -- exactly 2 round trips, then HMAC/expiry failure -- because both are syntactically well-formed JSON with the right key set; the requester's own tenant_id is what's resolved in both cases, never anything derived from the token's content. :crypto.hash_equals/2 (not simple ==) is itself constant-time, so the HMAC-mismatch branch does not leak via comparison timing either. Conclusion: no material AC4-relevant timing signal.
    - Response headers: read send_problem/2 (response.ex L115-122) and send_attachment_content/3 (instances.ex L1211-1216) -- the 410 path (send_problem) only ever calls put_resp_content_type(application/problem+json); it is the SAME single call site used for every other problem-document response in this codebase (not_found, internal_error, etc.), so no header distinguishes an expired-or-invalid response by cause. No put_resp_header call exists anywhere in the verify_link_token/check_attachment_id_matches/AttachmentLinks.verify code paths.
    - Status code: every branch inside AttachmentLinks.verify/3 and check_attachment_id_matches/2 maps to the identical 410 (Response.attachment_link_expired/1) -- confirmed no branch anywhere in handle_get_attachment_link_content/3's else clauses maps a token-verification failure to any status other than 410. (A DIFFERENT status, 404, is reachable from this same handler -- but only via fetch_scoped_attachment_content/3, which runs strictly AFTER a token has already verified successfully against the caller's own tenant key and matched its own URL attachment_id. Reaching that 404 branch requires having already produced a token that passes HMAC verification under the requester's own tenant's signing key -- i.e., the caller (or someone who leaked their token) was already the party the link was issued to. An attacker who was never issued a token for that tenant cannot reach this branch at all: any token they fabricate or replay cross-tenant fails verify/3 first and lands on 410, never touching fetch_scoped_attachment_content/3. So the 404-vs-410 split does not let a cross-tenant prober distinguish 'exists, not yours' from 'never existed' -- it only distinguishes, for someone who ALREADY holds a validly-signed-for-their-own-tenant token, 'attachment still present' from 'attachment deleted/instance-mismatched since issuance', which is not the class of probe INV-5/AC4 protects against, and mirrors the pre-existing, previously-reviewed 404 semantics of the original content route.)

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) -- APPLIES, SATISFIED by this review itself: (a)/(b)/(c) above are the explicit re-derivation this invariant requires, and this handoff's status:PASS with the full INV-1..INV-9 list is the proof artifact.

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES, SATISFIED. `grep -rn "Repo.query" lib/letflow/repository/attachment_links.ex lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex` returned zero hits. AttachmentLinks touches the DB only via Letflow.Secrets.resolve/2 and Letflow.Secrets.put/1 (already-reviewed, parameterized Ecto.Query calls per lib/letflow/secrets.ex L299-305's own from/2 usage) and Letflow.Identity.get_tenant/1. No raw SQL anywhere in this diff.

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES, SATISFIED. Every public function in attachment_links.ex returns a tagged tuple ({:ok,_}|{:error,_}); the second verify/3 clause (L155) catches any non-binary/non-list-opts call shape defensively. `grep -n "^\s*{:ok, .*} = "` against both new files returned two hits, both false positives on manual read -- both are `case` branch RETURN expressions (`{:ok, attachment, artifact} -> ...`), not bare `=` matches that could raise. Jason.decode/1 (non-bang, confirmed by reading the actual call site) returns {:error, _} rather than raising on malformed JSON, per Jason's own documented contract -- verify/3's guarded `with` clause correctly treats that as a non-match rather than relying on decode/1 to raise. verify_link_token/2's is_binary(link_token) guard (L1333) prevents a non-string query-param value (or its absence, which conn.query_params["link_token"] yields as nil) from ever reaching AttachmentLinks.verify/3 with a shape it doesn't handle.

INV-9 (tenant-controlled outbound URL validation) -- NOT APPLICABLE. This diff makes no outbound HTTP/HTTPS request of any kind (confirmed: no :httpc, no UrlValidator reference, no webhook dispatch touched).

Additional checks per task instructions:
  key_id namespace binding: pinned_reference/2 (attachment_links.ex L224-226) constructs "sec://tenant/#{tenant_slug}/#{@link_secret_namespace}/#{@link_secret_name}##{key_id}" -- @link_secret_namespace ("attachments") and @link_secret_name ("link_signing_key") are compile-time module attributes, never interpolated from caller/token input; key_id is the only token-derived segment, and it is already type-guarded to is_integer/1 by verify/3's decode pattern (L143), then interpolated via Elixir's default Integer-to-string conversion, which can only ever produce ASCII digits -- matching Letflow.Secrets' own reference regex `#(\\d+)` (secrets.ex L236). A crafted key_id therefore selects only a different KEY VERSION of the same fixed namespace/name pair for the caller's own tenant -- it cannot reference any other namespace or secret name. Secrets.resolve/2 additionally re-derives and checks the tenant from the reference's own tenant_slug (L291-297) independently of the caller-supplied key_id, so key_id has no path to any other tenant's data either.
  expires_at tamper-resistance: the signature in issue/3 is computed as sign(signing_key, payload) where `payload` is the exact Jason.encode!/1 output string containing expires_at (L102-109); verify/3 recomputes sign(signing_key, payload) over the exact raw decoded payload bytes (the Base.url_decode64/2 output, L140/147) -- never a re-serialization of the parsed map -- before comparing to the transmitted signature via :crypto.hash_equals/2 (L147). Any tamper to the expires_at digits inside the base64-decoded JSON payload changes those raw bytes, which changes the HMAC-SHA256 output, which fails the hash_equals/2 comparison and falls into the same else -> {:error, :expired_or_invalid} path -- confirmed no path exists where a tampered expires_at could reach the `expires_at > DateTime.to_unix(now)` check (L148) without first surviving an unmodified signature check over the tampered bytes.

No applicable invariant failed. No BLOCKER found.
issues: NON-BLOCKING, for DOC-UPDATER/ORCH: docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md's 'Applicability note' still describes INV-2/INV-5 as gated on 'S4 not started', which is stale -- S4's API surface has shipped extensively (Letflow.Api.Authorization's endpoint_policy_key/2 table alone lists ~50 live routes, and Letflow.Api.Error's own moduledoc already documents REQ-072's INV-5 mechanism as production behavior). This review applied INV-2/INV-5 as live per this task's own explicit instruction and per the actual state of the codebase, consistent with how INV-1's identical staleness was corrected in the 2026-08-17 addendum to the same file. Recommend the same kind of correcting addendum be made to the 'Applicability note' section for INV-2/INV-5.
